text: I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No man cometh to the Father, but by me.
author: Jesus Christ

text: Come to me, all you that labour, and are burdened, and I will refresh you.
author: Jesus Christ

text: I am the light of the world: he that followeth me, walketh not in darkness, but shall have the light of life.
author: Jesus Christ

text: This is my commandment, that you love one another, as I have loved you.
author: Jesus Christ

text: Blessed are the clean of heart: for they shall see God.
author: Jesus Christ

text: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called children of God.
author: Jesus Christ

text: Seek ye therefore first the kingdom of God, and his justice, and all these things shall be added unto you.
author: Jesus Christ

text: Ask, and it shall be given you: seek, and you shall find: knock, and it shall be opened to you.
author: Jesus Christ

text: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and behold I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world.
author: Jesus Christ

text: I am the resurrection and the life: he that believeth in me, although he be dead, shall live.
author: Jesus Christ

text: I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall not hunger: and he that believeth in me shall never thirst.
author: Jesus Christ

text: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd giveth his life for his sheep.
author: Jesus Christ

text: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, do I give unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, nor let it be afraid.
author: Jesus Christ

text: I am the vine: you the branches: he that abideth in me, and I in him, the same beareth much fruit: for without me you can do nothing.
author: Jesus Christ

text: Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.
author: Jesus Christ

text: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart, and with thy whole soul, and with thy whole mind.
author: Jesus Christ

text: Amen I say to you, as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me.
author: Jesus Christ

text: With men it is impossible; but not with God: for all things are possible with God.
author: Jesus Christ

text: Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.
author: Jesus Christ

text: Because thou hast seen me, Thomas, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and have believed.
author: Jesus Christ

text: If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
author: Jesus Christ

text: God so loved the world, as to give his only begotten Son; that whosoever believeth in him, may not perish, but may have life everlasting.
author: Jesus Christ

text: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it done to me according to thy word.
author: The Blessed Virgin Mary

text: My soul doth magnify the Lord. And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.
author: The Blessed Virgin Mary

text: Because he that is mighty, hath done great things to me; and holy is his name.
author: The Blessed Virgin Mary

text: Whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye.
author: The Blessed Virgin Mary

text: Son, why hast thou done so to us? behold thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing.
author: The Blessed Virgin Mary

text: The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing.
author: Psalm 22 (23)

text: The Lord is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear? The Lord is the protector of my life: of whom shall I be afraid?
author: Psalm 26 (27)

text: Be still and see that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted in the earth.
author: Psalm 45 (46)

text: This is the day which the Lord hath made: let us be glad and rejoice therein.
author: Psalm 117 (118)

text: Thy word is a lamp to my feet, and a light to my paths.
author: Psalm 118 (119)

text: O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet: blessed is the man that hopeth in him.
author: Psalm 33 (34)

text: Create a clean heart in me, O God: and renew a right spirit within my bowels.
author: Psalm 50 (51)

text: Fear not, for I am with thee: turn not aside, for I am thy God: I have strengthened thee, and have helped thee, and the right hand of my just one hath upheld thee.
author: The prophet Isaias

text: They that hope in the Lord shall renew their strength, they shall take wings as eagles, they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint.
author: The prophet Isaias

text: Fear not, for I have redeemed thee, and called thee by thy name: thou art mine.
author: The prophet Isaias

text: Can a woman forget her infant, so as not to have pity on the son of her womb? and if she should forget, yet will not I forget thee.
author: The prophet Isaias

text: I know the thoughts that I think towards you, saith the Lord, thoughts of peace, and not of affliction, to give you an end and patience.
author: The prophet Jeremias

text: The mercies of the Lord that we are not consumed: because his commiserations have not failed. They are new every morning, great is thy faithfulness.
author: Lamentations

text: Have confidence in the Lord with all thy heart, and lean not upon thy own prudence.
author: Proverbs

text: Behold I command thee, take courage, and be strong. Fear not and be not dismayed: because the Lord thy God is with thee in all things whatsoever thou shalt go to.
author: The Book of Josue

text: We know that to them that love God, all things work together unto good, to such as, according to his purpose, are called to be saints.
author: Saint Paul

text: What shall we then say to these things? If God be for us, who is against us?
author: Saint Paul

text: Be not overcome by evil, but overcome evil by good.
author: Saint Paul

text: Now there remain faith, hope, and charity, these three: but the greatest of these is charity.
author: Saint Paul

text: My grace is sufficient for thee; for power is made perfect in infirmity. Gladly therefore will I glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may dwell in me.
author: Saint Paul

text: I live, now not I; but Christ liveth in me. And that I live now in the flesh: I live in the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and delivered himself for me.
author: Saint Paul

text: Rejoice in the Lord always; again, I say, rejoice.
author: Saint Paul

text: I can do all these things in him who strengtheneth me.
author: Saint Paul

text: Pray without ceasing. In all things give thanks; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you all.
author: Saint Paul

text: Jesus Christ, yesterday, and to day; and the same for ever.
author: Letter to the Hebrews

text: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners: and purify your hearts, ye double minded.
author: Saint James

text: Casting all your care upon him, for he hath care of you.
author: Saint Peter

text: We have known, and have believed the charity, which God hath to us. God is charity: and he that abideth in charity, abideth in God, and God in him.
author: Saint John

text: Fear is not in charity: but perfect charity casteth out fear, because fear hath pain. And he that feareth, is not perfected in charity.
author: Saint John

text: I will shew thee, O man, what is good, and what the Lord requireth of thee: Verily, to do judgment, and to love mercy, and to walk solicitous with thy God.
author: The prophet Micheas

text: Believe God, and he will recover thee: and direct thy way, and trust in him. Keep his fear, and grow old therein.
author: Ecclesiasticus (Sirach)

text: Thou hast made us for thyself, O Lord, and our heart is restless until it rests in thee.
author: Saint Augustine of Hippo

text: Late have I loved thee, O Beauty ever ancient, ever new, late have I loved thee!
author: Saint Augustine of Hippo

text: Love, and do what you will.
author: Saint Augustine of Hippo
source: Homilies on the First Letter of John, 7.8

text: Ignorance of Scripture is ignorance of Christ.
author: Saint Jerome
source: Commentary on Isaiah, Prologue (quoted in CCC 133)

text: Where Peter is, there is the Church.
author: Saint Ambrose

text: He cannot have God for his Father who has not the Church for his mother.
author: Saint Cyprian of Carthage
source: On the Unity of the Catholic Church, 6

text: The glory of God is man fully alive; and the life of man is the vision of God.
author: Saint Irenaeus of Lyon

text: I am God’s wheat, and I am being ground by the teeth of wild beasts, that I may be found pure bread of Christ.
author: Saint Ignatius of Antioch

text: Eighty-six years have I served him, and he has done me no wrong. How then can I blaspheme my King who saved me?
author: Saint Polycarp of Smyrna

text: Listen, my son, to the precepts of the master, and incline the ear of your heart.
author: Saint Benedict

text: Let all guests who arrive be received like Christ.
author: Saint Benedict

text: Praised be you, my Lord, through Brother Sun, who brings the day; and you give light through him.
author: Saint Francis of Assisi

text: Lord, make me an instrument of your peace.
author: Traditional prayer in the spirit of Saint Francis

text: Grace does not destroy nature, but perfects it.
author: Saint Thomas Aquinas
source: Summa Theologiae, I, q. 1, a. 8, ad 2

text: Let nothing disturb you, let nothing frighten you. All things are passing; God never changes. Patience obtains all things. Whoever has God lacks nothing. God alone suffices.
author: Saint Teresa of Avila

text: Prayer, in my opinion, is nothing else than a close sharing between friends; it means taking time frequently to be alone with him who we know loves us.
author: Saint Teresa of Avila
source: The Book of Her Life, 8.5 (quoted in CCC 2709)

text: In the evening of life, we will be judged on love alone.
author: Saint John of the Cross
source: Sayings of Light and Love, 64 (quoted in CCC 1022)

text: My vocation, at last I have found it. My vocation is love!
author: Saint Thérèse of Lisieux
source: Story of a Soul, Manuscript B

text: For me, prayer is a surge of the heart; it is a simple look turned toward heaven, it is a cry of recognition and of love.
author: Saint Thérèse of Lisieux
source: Story of a Soul, Manuscript C (quoted in CCC 2558)

text: Prayer is the raising of one’s mind and heart to God or the requesting of good things from God.
author: Saint John Damascene
source: On the Orthodox Faith, 3.24 (quoted in CCC 2559)

text: My little children, your hearts are small, but prayer stretches them and makes them capable of loving God.
author: Saint John Vianney

text: Look to the star, call upon Mary.
author: Saint Bernard of Clairvaux

text: Remember, O most gracious Virgin Mary, that never was it known that anyone who fled to thy protection was left unaided.
author: The Memorare (attributed to Saint Bernard)

text: Jesus, I trust in you.
author: Saint Faustina Kowalska

text: Pray, hope, and don’t worry.
author: Saint Pio of Pietrelcina

text: The Eucharist is my highway to heaven.
author: Saint Carlo Acutis
source: Saying recorded by his family and friends

text: I die the king’s good servant, but God’s first.
author: Saint Thomas More

text: To live is to change, and to be perfect is to have changed often.
author: Saint John Henry Newman
source: An Essay on the Development of Christian Doctrine, chapter 1

text: Lead, kindly Light, amid the encircling gloom, lead thou me on!
author: Saint John Henry Newman

text: All for the greater glory of God.
author: Saint Ignatius of Loyola
source: Motto of the Society of Jesus (Ad maiorem Dei gloriam)

text: Take, Lord, and receive all my liberty, my memory, my understanding, and my entire will.
author: Saint Ignatius of Loyola

text: If you are what you should be, you will set all of Italy on fire.
author: Saint Catherine of Siena
source: Letter 368 (to Stefano Maconi); often quoted as “…set the world on fire”

text: To Jesus through Mary.
author: Saint Louis de Montfort

text: Death rather than sin.
author: Saint Dominic Savio

text: To the heights!
author: Saint Pier Giorgio Frassati
source: Written on a photograph of his last climb, 1925 (Verso l’alto)

text: Christ with me, Christ before me, Christ behind me, Christ in me, Christ beneath me, Christ above me.
author: Saint Patrick (traditional)

text: Do not be afraid! Open wide the doors for Christ!
author: Saint John Paul II
source: Homily at the Inauguration of his Pontificate, 22 October 1978

text: Faith and reason are like two wings on which the human spirit rises to the contemplation of truth.
author: Saint John Paul II

text: Man cannot live without love.
author: Saint John Paul II

text: The future of humanity passes by way of the family.
author: Saint John Paul II

text: Whoever believes is never alone, neither in life nor in death.
author: Pope Benedict XVI
source: Homily at the Mass for the Inauguration of his Pontificate, 24 April 2005

text: Being Christian is not the result of an ethical choice or a lofty idea, but the encounter with an event, a person.
author: Pope Benedict XVI

text: God is love, and he who abides in love abides in God, and God abides in him.
author: Pope Benedict XVI

text: Mercy is the very foundation of the Church’s life.
author: Pope Francis

text: The joy of the Gospel fills the hearts and lives of all who encounter Jesus.
author: Pope Francis

text: God never tires of forgiving us; we are the ones who tire of seeking his mercy.
author: Pope Francis

text: Peace be with you all!
author: Pope Leo XIV
source: First words from the loggia of Saint Peter’s, 8 May 2025

text: Peace on Earth, which men of every era have most eagerly yearned for, can be firmly established only if the order laid down by God be dutifully observed.
author: Saint John XXIII

text: Modern man listens more willingly to witnesses than to teachers, and if he does listen to teachers, it is because they are witnesses.
author: Saint Paul VI

text: The desire for God is written in the human heart, because man is created by God and for God.
author: Catechism of the Catholic Church

text: The Eucharist is the source and summit of the Christian life.
author: Second Vatican Council

text: The joys and the hopes, the griefs and the anxieties of the men of this age, especially those who are poor or in any way afflicted, these are the joys and hopes, the griefs and anxieties of the followers of Christ.
author: Second Vatican Council

text: All the faithful of Christ of whatever rank or status are called to the fullness of the Christian life and to the perfection of charity.
author: Second Vatican Council

text: The family is the domestic church.
author: Second Vatican Council
